deliveries.source: 48 kHz, 24-bit final mix with lossless normalized music and voice stems.

scope: Fresh technical channel, encoding, mono-compatibility and waveform checks. This is not a new subjective listening pass.
notes: Source AAC bitrate covers eight channels; it must not be interpreted as stereo-only bitrate.
A PCM intermediate preserves decoded samples but does not recover information removed by the original AAC recording.
Correlation identifies shared content and alignment; it does not alone rank perceptual quality.
conclusion: Retain the primary programme stereo feed for all 13 spoken cuts. The available original recordings are 48 kHz AAC; no uncompressed original programme master is present. The secondary recording provides the same programme feed plus separate microphone channels, rather than a higher-fidelity complete mix. The cuts preserve the selected programme feed through lossless 24-bit stereo intermediates and AAC-LC delivery encodes configured at 384 kbps.
limitations: This is a technical source and delivery audit combined with the user’s accepted playback review; no direct listening by the assistant is claimed.
Separate microphone tracks could support a different creative remix, but are not an identified higher-quality complete programme master.
Final AAC average bitrates vary with signal complexity; 384 kbps is the encoder target, not a claim that every second or file averages that rate.
